text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to managing projects, especially in software development. Instead of doing everything at once, teams work in short bursts called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. Each sprint begins with a planning session, where the team picks tasks from a list called the backlog. These tasks are often written as user stories, short descriptions that explain what a user wants and why it matters. Every day, the team has a quick standup meeting to share progress and flag any problems. Through iterative development, they deliver small improvements regularly, allowing them to adapt quickly to feedback and changing requirements.
